sources.entry: tox - Automatically builds and tests distributions in multiple Python versions.

summary.one_liner: tox is a command line tool that creates isolated virtual environments to automate and standardize testing and packaging checks for Python projects.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes tox as a generic virtual environment management and test command line tool. It is used to check that a package builds and installs correctly under different environments, such as different Python implementations, versions, or installation dependencies. It runs tests in each of those environments using the test tool the user chooses. It can also act as a frontend to continuous integration servers, reducing boilerplate and combining CI and shell-based testing. The README points to a user guide for configuration details, which is not included in the text provided.
use_cases: test a Python package across multiple Python versions
check that a package builds and installs correctly
run test suites in isolated virtual environments
reduce boilerplate in continuous integration configuration
standardize Python testing and release workflows
notable: Builds and tests packages in multiple Python environments from one command
Works as a frontend to CI servers, merging CI and shell-based testing
Part of a larger toolchain alongside pytest and devpi, per the README
Runs whatever test tool the user chooses in each environment
caveats: The README is short and defers setup and configuration details to an external user guide
Installation and run commands are not given in the README text provided
keywords: test python package on many versions
